title: Spec profile
description: One per specification: specs/<id>/spec.yaml. It names the specification, says how its schemas are produced, and gives the data the pipeline reads for it. A specification read from its text names the plugin under src/specs/<plugin>/ that holds its readers: its table layouts, its type and presence grammar, its value-list forms, and its section numbering. A schema set imported as published, with no text to extract, names no plugin.

id.description: Equals the folder's name under specs/.

title.description: The specification's name and version, as its owners write them.

front_end.description: How the pipeline reads the specification: `text`, extracted from the specification's text into the IR by its plugin, then mapped and emitted; or `schemas`, a published schema set read as it is, with no IR.

plugin.description: The plugin under src/specs/ that reads the specification's text.

documents.description: The documents the specification's field rows describe: each row's owner, found by the top-level section the row sits in, and the document it names, the owner in PascalCase.

section.description: The top-level section number whose field rows the owner has.

imports.description: The registry specs on this site whose code lists the spec takes, each at the one lock of it the spec pins, as OpenProposal takes AdCOM's lists at main. A list the spec cites comes from the registry's committed outputs at that lock, and its schemas reference the registry's, so the spec copies no code.

statements.description: Which sentences are statements with a level: `uppercase`, a sentence with an RFC 2119 keyword in capitals, as the specification's conventions say; or `any-case`, a sentence with a keyword in any case, for a specification that states no convention and writes its keywords in either case, as a decision records.

features.description: The parts of the pipeline the specification uses beyond its tables, rows, and statements. Each is off unless the profile turns it on, and the plugin must agree.

markers.description: Field rows carry a mutability marker, defined by a marker table.

appendices.description: Appendices restate the field rows, which the round trip checks.

profiles.description: The specification defines summary profiles of a document.

through.description: The last stage of the pipeline the spec has reached, for a spec still being added: `input`, its locks and snapshots; `extract`, its IR and findings; or `model`, its mapping, decisions, kernel binding, and model. CI runs its gates through that stage, and the spec's folder may hold no file of a later stage, and none that no stage writes. Left out, the spec has every stage, and every gate runs on it.

names.description: The names the outputs carry: the specification's name in prose, the base of every schema's `$id`, and the SDK packages.

short.description: The specification's name in prose, as in "the OpenProposal specification".

edition.description: The version people name it by, as in "OpenProposal 3.0".

release.description: The draft or release of the text the default lock pins, as in "OpenProposal 3.0 draft 1".

schema_base.description: The base of every schema's `$id`; the site serves each schema at its `$id`.

package.description: The Python package, which is also each tree's folder under `python/`.

mode_key.description: The validation context's key that sets the receive mode.

entry_points.description: The entry-point group extensions register under.

module.description: The repository's Go module path, which each tree's module path continues with its folder.

package.description: The Go package, which also prefixes every error the runtime returns.

sdk.description: The SDK packages, for a spec whose types the SDK emitters write; a spec without them has no SDK types.

site.description: The spec's pages on the public site (specs/site.yaml gives the site's host, publisher, and repository).

default_type.description: The type the type map opens at.

example.description: The field the How it's built page follows through each step, and the build its links open, for a spec whose page follows one.

locks.description: How the pages name each lock, by its name: a label for its switch, a short form for a table, the phrase that places a type or a record on it, and other names the type map's address may give it. A lock the map doesn't list is named by its name.

where.description: The phrase, as in "cited on main" or "cited with the open PRs".

aliases.description: Other names an address may give the lock, beside its name and its label's and short form's slugs.

registry.description: Whether the spec's vocabularies are a registry of code lists that other specs cite, as AdCOM's lists are; the site then gives it a page of every list and the specs that cite it.

feedback.description: The implementation feedback's target and its content: the issue the comment follows up on, the pull requests that are ours, and the groups and rows the report is laid out in.

issue.description: The issue the comment follows up on.

gist.description: The supporting page the comment links.

prs.description: The upstream pull requests we posted ourselves, which the inputs name as ours.

groups.description: The groups of decisions, in the order the pipeline cites them.

rules.description: The authoring rules the issue proposes, and the rows for the findings they don't cover, each with what it asks above its findings.

kinds.description: Each lint kind's row; the profile gate holds the table to every kind.

suggestion.description: A suggestion to the working group that no decision makes; a `{D-…}` stands for that decision's number.
